LESSON: SIGN READING 1.2.1 EXTENSIVE SIGN READING: REFERENCE MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Sign Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Reference Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Reference Materials, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to spell words correctly? 2. Why is it important to fingerspell words correctly? 3. How does a dictionary help us to learn?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Reference Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: Self-discipline as learner properly utilise reference materials as they identify the spelling and meaning of words.

● Digital literacy: Interacting with digital devices as learner uses digital devices to search for meaning of words and information from the web.

Values:
● Responsibility: Determination as learner collaborates with peers to perform various roles as they search for spelling and meaning of words.

● Integrity: Transparency as learners focus on specific information required of them when searching in online platforms.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate the concept of reading for information to their learning in Kiswahili.
